diff --git a/docs/querying/functions.md b/docs/querying/functions.md
index 68a0033..0fa4de8 100644
--- a/docs/querying/functions.md
+++ b/docs/querying/functions.md
@@ -816,8 +816,31 @@ label values are equal, elements are sorted by their full label sets.
 Please note that `sort_by_label` only affects the results of instant queries, as
 range query results always have a fixed output ordering.
 
-`sort_by_label` uses [natural sort
-order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_sort_order).
+Label values are compared by the kind of value they represent, so that e.g.
+`9s` sorts before `10s` and `192.168.0.9` before `192.168.0.10`. Values of
+different kinds are grouped, and the groups sort in the following order:
+
+1. Values starting with whitespace. Leading whitespace prevents a value from
+   being interpreted as any of the kinds below.
+1. Positive infinity (`Inf`, `+Inf`, `+infinity`, …).
+1. Numbers, including decimals and scientific notation (`-1`, `2.5`, `+1e3`, …).
+1. Negative infinity (`-Inf`, `-infinity`, …).
+1. Durations, i.e. a number followed by one of the units `ns`, `us`, `µs`,
+   `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`, `w` or `y` (`1.5h`, `-2e3ms`, …).
+1. Byte sizes, i.e. a number followed by one of the units `B`, `kB`, `MB`,
+   `GB`, `TB`, `PB`, `EB`, `ZB`, `YB`, `KiB`, `MiB`, `GiB`, `TiB`, `PiB`,
+   `EiB`, `ZiB` or `YiB`, matched case insensitively (`999B`, `1.5MiB`, …).
+1. [Semantic versions](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html) with an optional
+   leading `v` (`1.2.3`, `v2.0.0-rc.1`, …).
+1. IP addresses, IPv4 before IPv6 (`10.0.0.1`, `::1`, …).
+1. CIDR prefixes, IPv4 before IPv6 and, for the same network address, larger
+   networks first (`10.0.0.0/8`, `2001:db8::/32`, …).
+1. Timestamps, e.g. in RFC 3339 format (`2023-01-01T00:00:00Z`, …).
+1. All other values, including empty ones.
+
+Values that do not belong to any of the other groups, as well as values that
+are equal within their group, are sorted by [natural sort
+order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_sort_order) of their label values.
 
 ## `sort_by_label_desc()`

diff --git a/util/labelsort/decimal.go b/util/labelsort/decimal.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..5926e9a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/util/labelsort/decimal.go
@@ -0,0 +1,194 @@
+// Copyright The Prometheus Authors
+// Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
+// you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
+// You may obtain a copy of the License at
+//
+// http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
+//
+// Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
+// distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
+// WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+// See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+// limitations under the License.
+
+package labelsort
+
+import (
+	"cmp"
+	"math/big"
+	"strings"
+)
+
+// decimal is an exact decimal number of the form ±0.digits × 10^exp.
+//
+// digits never contains leading or trailing zeros, which makes the
+// representation canonical: an empty digits string means the number is zero,
+// and for everything else the exponent alone gives the order of magnitude.
+// Numbers are therefore compared by their exponent first and by their digits
+// second, without ever converting them to a float and losing precision.
+type decimal struct {
+	neg    bool
+	digits string
+	exp    int64
+}
+
+// Exponents are clamped rather than allowed to overflow. Numbers beyond that
+// range cannot be told apart, which only means that they compare equal and are
+// then ordered by the natural order of their original strings, so the overall
+// ordering stays total.
+const (
+	maxExp      = int64(1) << 61
+	minExp      = -maxExp
+	maxExpInput = int64(1) << 59
+)
+
+func (d decimal) isZero() bool { return d.digits == "" }
+
+// parseDecimalPrefix parses the longest decimal number at the start of s and
+// returns it along with the remainder of s. Numbers have an optional sign, an
+// integer and/or a fractional part and an optional decimal exponent. Anything
+// that is not part of a complete number is left in the remainder: "1e" parses
+// as the number 1 with the remainder "e".
+func parseDecimalPrefix(s string) (decimal, string, bool) {
+	i := 0
+	neg := false
+	if i < len(s) && (s[i] == '+' || s[i] == '-') {
+		neg = s[i] == '-'
+		i++
+	}
+
+	intStart := i
+	for i < len(s) && isDigit(s[i]) {
+		i++
+	}
+	intDigits := s[intStart:i]
+
+	fracDigits := ""
+	if i < len(s) && s[i] == '.' && i+1 < len(s) && isDigit(s[i+1]) {
+		fracStart := i + 1
+		i = fracStart
+		for i < len(s) && isDigit(s[i]) {
+			i++
+		}
+		fracDigits = s[fracStart:i]
+	}
+	if intDigits == "" && fracDigits == "" {
+		return decimal{}, s, false
+	}
+
+	exp := int64(0)
+	if i < len(s) && (s[i] == 'e' || s[i] == 'E') {
+		j := i + 1
+		expNeg := false
+		if j < len(s) && (s[j] == '+' || s[j] == '-') {
+			expNeg = s[j] == '-'
+			j++
+		}
+		expStart := j
+		for j < len(s) && isDigit(s[j]) {
+			j++
+		}
+		if j > expStart {
+			exp = parseExp(s[expStart:j], expNeg)
+			i = j
+		}
+	}
+
+	return newDecimal(neg, intDigits, fracDigits, exp), s[i:], true
+}
+
+// newDecimal normalizes the parts of a parsed number into a decimal.
+func newDecimal(neg bool, intDigits, fracDigits string, exp int64) decimal {
+	digits := intDigits + fracDigits
+	// digits × 10^(exp-len(fracDigits)) is 0.digits × 10^e.
+	e := addExp(exp, int64(len(digits))-int64(len(fracDigits)))
+
+	// Dropping a leading zero shifts the digits one place to the left.
+	lead := 0
+	for lead < len(digits) && digits[lead] == '0' {
+		lead++
+	}
+	digits = digits[lead:]
+	e = addExp(e, -int64(lead))
+
+	// Trailing zeros carry no information in the 0.digits form.
+	digits = strings.TrimRight(digits, "0")
+	if digits == "" {
+		return decimal{}
+	}
+	return decimal{neg: neg, digits: digits, exp: e}
+}
+
+// mul returns d scaled by the factor f, which must be positive.
+func (d decimal) mul(f decimal) decimal {
+	switch {
+	case d.isZero() || f.isZero():
+		return decimal{}
+	case f.digits == "1":
+		return decimal{neg: d.neg, digits: d.digits, exp: addExp(d.exp, f.exp-1)}
+	}
+	p := new(big.Int).Mul(digitsToInt(d.digits), digitsToInt(f.digits))
+	digits := p.String()
+	e := addExp(addExp(d.exp, f.exp), int64(len(digits)-len(d.digits)-len(f.digits)))
+	return decimal{neg: d.neg, digits: strings.TrimRight(digits, "0"), exp: e}
+}
+
+// compareDecimals compares two decimals by value.
+func compareDecimals(a, b decimal) int {
+	switch {
+	case a.isZero() && b.isZero():
+		return 0
+	case a.isZero():
+		if b.neg {
+			return 1
+		}
+		return -1
+	case b.isZero():
+		if a.neg {
+			return -1
+		}
+		return 1
+	case a.neg != b.neg:
+		if a.neg {
+			return -1
+		}
+		return 1
+	}
+
+	c := cmp.Compare(a.exp, b.exp)
+	if c == 0 {
+		// Both digit strings start with a non-zero digit, so the shorter one is
+		// smaller whenever it is a prefix of the longer one.
+		c = strings.Compare(a.digits, b.digits)
+	}
+	if a.neg {
+		return -c
+	}
+	return c
+}
+
+func digitsToInt(digits string) *big.Int {
+	i, _ := new(big.Int).SetString(digits, 10)
+	return i
+}
+
+// parseExp turns the digits of an exponent into a number, clamping values that
+// are too large to be represented.
+func parseExp(digits string, neg bool) int64 {
+	v := int64(0)
+	for i := 0; i < len(digits) && v <= maxExpInput; i++ {
+		v = v*10 + int64(digits[i]-'0')
+	}
+	v = min(v, maxExpInput)
+	if neg {
+		return -v
+	}
+	return v
+}
+
+// addExp adds two exponents, clamping the result to the representable range.
+func addExp(a, b int64) int64 {
+	return min(max(a+b, minExp), maxExp)
+}
+
+func isDigit(c byte) bool { return c >= '0' && c <= '9' }

@@ -0,0 +1,124 @@
+// Copyright The Prometheus Authors

+package labelsort
+
+import (
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+func TestParseDecimalPrefix(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, c := range []struct {
+		in   string
+		want decimal
+		rest string
+		ok   bool
+	}{
+		{in: "0", want: decimal{}, ok: true},
+		{in: "-0.000", want: decimal{}, ok: true},
+		{in: "1", want: decimal{digits: "1", exp: 1}, ok: true},
+		{in: "+1", want: decimal{digits: "1", exp: 1}, ok: true},
+		{in: "-1", want: decimal{neg: true, digits: "1", exp: 1}, ok: true},
+		{in: "10", want: decimal{digits: "1", exp: 2}, ok: true},
+		{in: "0.5", want: decimal{digits: "5", exp: 0}, ok: true},
+		{in: ".5", want: decimal{digits: "5", exp: 0}, ok: true},
+		{in: "0.0500", want: decimal{digits: "5", exp: -1}, ok: true},
+		{in: "1.5", want: decimal{digits: "15", exp: 1}, ok: true},
+		{in: "1e3", want: decimal{digits: "1", exp: 4}, ok: true},
+		{in: "1E+3", want: decimal{digits: "1", exp: 4}, ok: true},
+		{in: "1e-3", want: decimal{digits: "1", exp: -2}, ok: true},
+		{in: "-1.5e2", want: decimal{neg: true, digits: "15", exp: 3}, ok: true},
+		// Incomplete parts are left in the remainder.
+		{in: "1e", want: decimal{digits: "1", exp: 1}, rest: "e", ok: true},
+		{in: "1e+", want: decimal{digits: "1", exp: 1}, rest: "e+", ok: true},
+		{in: "1.", want: decimal{digits: "1", exp: 1}, rest: ".", ok: true},
+		{in: "1.2.3", want: decimal{digits: "12", exp: 1}, rest: ".3", ok: true},
+		{in: "1e3ms", want: decimal{digits: "1", exp: 4}, rest: "ms", ok: true},
+		{in: "1eb", want: decimal{digits: "1", exp: 1}, rest: "eb", ok: true},
+		// Not numbers at all.
+		{in: "", rest: "", ok: false},
+		{in: "abc", rest: "abc", ok: false},
+		{in: "+", rest: "+", ok: false},
+		{in: ".", rest: ".", ok: false},
+		{in: " 1", rest: " 1", ok: false},
+	} {
+		t.Run(c.in, func(t *testing.T) {
+			d, rest, ok := parseDecimalPrefix(c.in)
+			require.Equal(t, c.ok, ok)
+			if !ok {
+				require.Equal(t, c.rest, rest)
+				return
+			}
+			require.Equal(t, c.want, d)
+			require.Equal(t, c.rest, rest)
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+func TestCompareDecimals(t *testing.T) {
+	values := []string{
+		"-1e3", "-999.5", "-1", "-0.001", "0", "0.001", "1", "1.0000000000000000001",
+		"999.5", "1e3", "1e1000", "1e" + strings.Repeat("9", 30),
+	}
+	for i, a := range values {
+		for j, b := range values {
+			da, _, ok := parseDecimalPrefix(a)
+			require.True(t, ok)
+			db, _, ok := parseDecimalPrefix(b)
+			require.True(t, ok)
+
+			want := 0
+			switch {
+			case i < j:
+				want = -1
+			case i > j:
+				want = 1
+			}
+			require.Equalf(t, want, compareDecimals(da, db), "comparing %q and %q", a, b)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func TestDecimalMul(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, c := range []struct{ in, factor, want string }{
+		{in: "1", factor: "1", want: "1"},
+		{in: "1", factor: "1e9", want: "1e9"},
+		{in: "1.5", factor: "60e9", want: "9e10"},
+		{in: "-2", factor: "1024", want: "-2048"},
+		{in: "0", factor: "1e9", want: "0"},
+		{in: "1e1000", factor: "1208925819614629174706176", want: "1208925819614629174706176e1000"},
+	} {
+		t.Run(c.in+"*"+c.factor, func(t *testing.T) {
+			got := mustParseDecimal(c.in).mul(mustParseDecimal(c.factor))
+			require.Equal(t, 0, compareDecimals(mustParseDecimal(c.want), got))
+			require.Equal(t, mustParseDecimal(c.want), got)
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+// TestDecimalExponentClamping makes sure that exponents beyond the
+// representable range keep the comparison usable instead of overflowing.
+func TestDecimalExponentClamping(t *testing.T) {
+	huge := "1e" + strings.Repeat("9", 40)
+	tiny := "1e-" + strings.Repeat("9", 40)
+
+	require.Equal(t, +1, Compare(huge, "1e1000000"))
+	require.Equal(t, -1, Compare(tiny, "1e-1000000"))
+	require.Equal(t, -1, Compare(tiny, huge))
+	// Values that both clamp cannot be told apart, so their strings decide.
+	require.Equal(t, -1, Compare("1e"+strings.Repeat("9", 40), "2e"+strings.Repeat("9", 40)))
+	require.Equal(t, +1, Compare("2e"+strings.Repeat("9", 40), "1e"+strings.Repeat("9", 40)))
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,239 @@
+// Copyright The Prometheus Authors
+// Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
+// you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
+// You may obtain a copy of the License at
+//
+// http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
+//
+// Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
+// distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
+// WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+// See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+// limitations under the License.
+
+// Package labelsort implements the ordering used for sorting label values.
+//
+// Label values are plain strings, but they usually carry a value of a more
+// specific domain, like a number, a duration, a size, a version or an address.
+// Compare recognizes those domains and orders values of the same domain by
+// their meaning rather than by their string representation, so that e.g. "9s"
+// sorts before "10s" and "192.168.0.9" before "192.168.0.10".
+//
+// Values of different domains are ordered by their domain, in the order given
+// by the class constants below, and values that are equal within their domain
+// are ordered by the natural order of their original strings. The resulting
+// order is total: Compare only returns 0 for identical strings.
+package labelsort
+
+import (
+	"cmp"
+	"net/netip"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+	"unicode"
+	"unicode/utf8"
+)
+
+// class is the domain a label value belongs to. The order of the constants is
+// the order in which values of the different domains sort.
+type class int
+
+const (
+	// whitespaceValue is a value starting with whitespace. Such values are
+	// never interpreted as a typed value, as the leading whitespace makes them
+	// too likely to mean something else than they look like.
+	whitespaceValue class = iota
+	positiveInfinity
+	number
+	negativeInfinity
+	duration
+	byteSize
+	semanticVersion
+	ipAddress
+	cidrPrefix
+	timestamp
+	// plainString is a value that does not belong to any other domain,
+	// including the empty value.
+	plainString
+)
+
+// timeLayouts are the timestamp formats that are recognized, most specific
+// first. Layouts without a time zone are interpreted as UTC.
+var timeLayouts = []string{
+	time.RFC3339Nano, // Covers RFC3339 as well, as fractional seconds are optional when parsing.
+	"2006-01-02T15:04:05.999999999",
+	"2006-01-02 15:04:05.999999999Z07:00",
+	"2006-01-02 15:04:05.999999999",
+	"2006-01-02",
+	time.RFC1123Z,
+	time.RFC1123,
+}
+
+// minTimestampLen is the length of the shortest recognized timestamp, used to
+// skip the timestamp parsing for values that cannot be one.
+const minTimestampLen = len("2006-01-02")
+
+// value is a label value parsed into its domain.
+type value struct {
+	class class
+	num   decimal      // number, duration and byteSize.
+	ver   semver       // semanticVersion.
+	addr  netip.Addr   // ipAddress.
+	pfx   netip.Prefix // cidrPrefix.
+	time  time.Time    // timestamp.
+}
+
+// Compare returns -1 if the label value a sorts before b, +1 if it sorts after
+// b, and 0 if a and b are the same value.
+func Compare(a, b string) int {
+	if a == b {
+		return 0
+	}
+	va, vb := parse(a), parse(b)
+	if c := cmp.Compare(va.class, vb.class); c != 0 {
+		return c
+	}
+	if c := va.compare(vb); c != 0 {
+		return c
+	}
+	// Values that carry no typed information, or that are equal within their
+	// domain but spelled differently, are ordered by the natural order of their
+	// original strings. Strings that are also equal naturally, like "01" and
+	// "1", are ordered by their bytes to keep the order total.
+	if c := naturalCompare(a, b); c != 0 {
+		return c
+	}
+	return strings.Compare(a, b)
+}
+
+// Less reports whether the label value a sorts before b.
+func Less(a, b string) bool { return Compare(a, b) < 0 }
+
+// compare compares two values of the same class.
+func (v value) compare(o value) int {
+	switch v.class {
+	case number, duration, byteSize:
+		return compareDecimals(v.num, o.num)
+	case semanticVersion:
+		return compareSemvers(v.ver, o.ver)
+	case ipAddress:
+		// Addr.Compare sorts IPv4 addresses before IPv6 addresses and
+		// IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses with the latter.
+		return v.addr.Compare(o.addr)
+	case cidrPrefix:
+		if c := v.pfx.Addr().Compare(o.pfx.Addr()); c != 0 {
+			return c
+		}
+		// Prefixes of the same network sort from the largest to the smallest
+		// network. (Prefix.Compare is not used here, as it orders by prefix
+		// length before it orders by address.)
+		return cmp.Compare(v.pfx.Bits(), o.pfx.Bits())
+	case timestamp:
+		return v.time.Compare(o.time)
+	}
+	// Values of the remaining classes are either all equal (the infinities) or
+	// carry no typed value at all.
+	return 0
+}
+
+// parse determines the domain of a label value and parses it.
+func parse(s string) value {
+	if r, _ := utf8.DecodeRuneInString(s); unicode.IsSpace(r) {
+		return value{class: whitespaceValue}
+	}
+	if v, ok := parseNumber(s); ok {
+		return v
+	}
+	if d, ok := parseScaled(s, durationUnits, false); ok {
+		return value{class: duration, num: d}
+	}
+	if d, ok := parseScaled(s, byteUnits, true); ok {
+		return value{class: byteSize, num: d}
+	}
+	if ver, ok := parseSemver(s); ok {
+		return value{class: semanticVersion, ver: ver}
+	}
+	if looksLikeAddr(s) {
+		if addr, err := netip.ParseAddr(s); err == nil {
+			return value{class: ipAddress, addr: addr}
+		}
+		if pfx, err := netip.ParsePrefix(s); err == nil {
+			return value{class: cidrPrefix, pfx: pfx}
+		}
+	}
+	if t, ok := parseTimestamp(s); ok {
+		return value{class: timestamp, time: t}
+	}
+	return value{class: plainString}
+}
+
+// parseNumber parses a number, including the infinities. NaN is not a number
+// here: it has no place in an ordering, so it is left to sort as a string.
+func parseNumber(s string) (value, bool) {
+	if c, ok := parseInfinity(s); ok {
+		return value{class: c}, true
+	}
+	d, rest, ok := parseDecimalPrefix(s)
+	if !ok || rest != "" {
+		return value{}, false
+	}
+	return value{class: number, num: d}, true
+}
+
+func parseInfinity(s string) (class, bool) {
+	neg := false
+	if s != "" && (s[0] == '+' || s[0] == '-') {
+		neg = s[0] == '-'
+		s = s[1:]
+	}
+	if !strings.EqualFold(s, "inf") && !strings.EqualFold(s, "infinity") {
+		return 0, false
+	}
+	if neg {
+		return negativeInfinity, true
+	}
+	return positiveInfinity, true
+}
+
+func parseTimestamp(s string) (time.Time, bool) {
+	if len(s) < minTimestampLen || !looksLikeTimestamp(s) {
+		return time.Time{}, false
+	}
+	for _, layout := range timeLayouts {
+		if t, err := time.Parse(layout, s); err == nil {
+			return t, true
+		}
+	}
+	return time.Time{}, false
+}
+
+// looksLikeAddr reports whether s could be an IP address or a CIDR prefix.
+// Failing to parse one allocates, so values that obviously are neither are
+// filtered out first: both always contain a dot or a colon and start with a
+// hexadecimal digit or a colon.
+func looksLikeAddr(s string) bool {
+	if s == "" || !isHexDigit(s[0]) && s[0] != ':' {
+		return false
+	}
+	return strings.ContainsAny(s, ".:")
+}
+
+func isHexDigit(c byte) bool {
+	return isDigit(c) || c >= 'a' && c <= 'f' || c >= 'A' && c <= 'F'
+}
+
+// looksLikeTimestamp reports whether s could be a timestamp, which saves the
+// parsing attempts for the vast majority of values that cannot be one. All
+// recognized layouts start either with a four digit year followed by a hyphen
+// or with an abbreviated weekday followed by a comma.
+func looksLikeTimestamp(s string) bool {
+	if s[3] == ',' {
+		return true
+	}
+	for i := range 4 {
+		if !isDigit(s[i]) {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return s[4] == '-'
+}

+// Copyright The Prometheus Authors

+
+package labelsort
+
+import (
+	"math/rand"
+	"slices"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+// sortedValues lists label values in the order in which they have to sort,
+// from the first to the last. Every value is strictly smaller than all values
+// following it.
+var sortedValues = []string{
+	// Values starting with whitespace are never typed and sort before
+	// everything else, in natural order.
+	"\t5",
+	" ",
+	" +Inf",
+	" 2",
+	" 2m",
+	" 10",
+
+	// Positive infinity, before all finite numbers.
+	"+Inf",
+	"+inf",
+	"Inf",
+	"infinity",
+
+	// Finite numbers.
+	"-1e3",
+	"-2",
+	"-1.5",
+	"-0.5",
+	"+0",
+	"-0",
+	"0",
+	".5",
+	"0.50",
+	"0.5000000000000000000000001",
+	"01",
+	"1",
+	"1.5",
+	"+2",
+	"10",
+	"1e3",
+	"9007199254740992",
+	"9007199254740993",
+	"1e400",
+	"2e400",
+
+	// Negative infinity, after all finite numbers.
+	"-Inf",
+	"-inf",
+
+	// Durations.
+	"-1h",
+	"-1e3ms",
+	"0s",
+	"1ns",
+	"1us",
+	"1µs",
+	"1ms",
+	"500ms",
+	"1s",
+	"1.5s",
+	"90s",
+	"2m",
+	"1h",
+	"1.5h",
+	"1d",
+	"1w",
+	"1y",
+	"1e30y",
+	"2e30y",
+
+	// Byte sizes.
+	"-1MB",
+	"0B",
+	"1B",
+	"999B",
+	"1KB",
+	"1kb",
+	"1KiB",
+	"1MB",
+	"1MiB",
+	"1GiB",
+	"1TB",
+	"1e30YiB",
+	"2e30YiB",
+
+	// Semantic versions.
+	"0.1.0",
+	"v1.0.0-alpha",
+	"1.0.0-alpha.1",
+	"1.0.0-alpha.beta",
+	"1.0.0-beta",
+	"1.0.0-rc.1",
+	"1.0.0-rc.2",
+	"1.0.0",
+	"1.0.0+build.1",
+	"v1.0.0",
+	"1.2.3",
+	"1.11.3",
+	"1.111.3",
+	"2.0.0",
+	"10.0.0",
+
+	// IP addresses, IPv4 before IPv6.
+	"0.0.0.0",
+	"10.0.0.2",
+	"10.0.0.10",
+	"192.168.1.1",
+	"255.255.255.255",
+	"::",
+	"::1",
+	"::ffff:1.2.3.4", // An IPv4-mapped IPv6 address is an IPv6 address.
+	"2001:db8::1",
+	"fe80::1",
+
+	// CIDR prefixes, IPv4 before IPv6 and larger networks first.
+	"0.0.0.0/0",
+	"10.0.0.0/8",
+	"10.0.0.0/16",
+	"10.0.0.0/24",
+	"10.1.0.0/16",
+	"192.168.0.0/24",
+	"::/0",
+	"2001:db8::/32",
+	"fe80::/10",
+
+	// Timestamps.
+	"2023-01-01",
+	"2023-01-01T00:00:00Z",
+	"2023-01-01T00:00:00.5Z",
+	"2023-06-01T12:00:00+02:00",
+	"2023-06-01 12:00:00",
+	"Mon, 02 Jan 2034 15:04:05 UTC",
+
+	// Everything else, in natural order.
+	"",
+	"-",
+	"1e",
+	"4m5",
+	"4m600",
+	"4m1000",
+	"10.0.0.256",
+	"NaN",
+	"canary",
+	"foo1",
+	"foo2",
+	"foo10",
+	"production",
+	"v1.2",
+}
+
+func TestCompareOrder(t *testing.T) {
+	for i, a := range sortedValues {
+		for j, b := range sortedValues {
+			switch {
+			case i < j:
+				require.Equalf(t, -1, Compare(a, b), "expected %q to sort before %q", a, b)
+			case i > j:
+				require.Equalf(t, +1, Compare(a, b), "expected %q to sort after %q", a, b)
+			default:
+				require.Equalf(t, 0, Compare(a, b), "expected %q to be equal to itself", a)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func TestCompareSorts(t *testing.T) {
+	shuffled := slices.Clone(sortedValues)
+	rnd := rand.New(rand.NewSource(42))
+	for range 10 {
+		rnd.Shuffle(len(shuffled), func(i, j int) {
+			shuffled[i], shuffled[j] = shuffled[j], shuffled[i]
+		})
+		// An unstable sort only produces a deterministic result if the
+		// comparison is a total order.
+		slices.SortFunc(shuffled, Compare)
+		require.Equal(t, sortedValues, shuffled)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestLess(t *testing.T) {
+	require.True(t, Less("9s", "10s"))
+	require.False(t, Less("10s", "9s"))
+	require.False(t, Less("10s", "10s"))
+}
+
+func TestParseClass(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, c := range []struct {
+		value string
+		class class
+	}{
+		{" 1", whitespaceValue},
+		{"\n1", whitespaceValue},
+		{" 1", whitespaceValue}, // Non-breaking space.
+		{"+Inf", positiveInfinity},
+		{"INFINITY", positiveInfinity},
+		{"-Inf", negativeInfinity},
+		{"-infinity", negativeInfinity},
+		{"1", number},
+		{"+1", number},
+		{"-1", number},
+		{".5", number},
+		{"1.5", number},
+		{"1e3", number},
+		{"1E-3", number},
+		{"+1.5e+3", number},
+		{"1e", plainString},   // A bare exponent marker is not a number.
+		{"1e+", plainString},  // Neither is an exponent without digits.
+		{"NaN", plainString},  // NaN has no place in an ordering.
+		{"-nan", plainString}, //
+		{"1.", plainString},   // A fractional part needs at least one digit.
+		{"1 ", plainString},   // Trailing whitespace is not trimmed.
+		{"0x1f", plainString}, // Only decimal numbers are recognized.
+		{"1ns", duration},
+		{"1us", duration},
+		{"1µs", duration},
+		{"1μs", duration},
+		{"1ms", duration},
+		{"-1.5s", duration},
+		{"+1m", duration},
+		{"1e3h", duration},
+		{"1d", duration},
+		{"1w", duration},
+		{"1y", duration},
+		{"1S", plainString}, // Duration units are case sensitive.
+		{"1h30m", plainString},
+		{"1B", byteSize},
+		{"1b", byteSize},
+		{"-1.5kB", byteSize},
+		{"+1e3MiB", byteSize},
+		{"1YB", byteSize},
+		{"1yib", byteSize},
+		{"1K", plainString}, // Byte units need the B.
+		{"1.2.3", semanticVersion},
+		{"v1.2.3", semanticVersion},
+		{"1.2.3-rc.1", semanticVersion},
+		{"1.2.3+build", semanticVersion},
+		{"1.2.3-rc.1+build", semanticVersion},
+		// Semantic versions need exactly three numeric parts.
+		{"v1.2", plainString},
+		{"1.2.3.4", ipAddress},
+		{"v1.2.3.4", plainString},
+		// No leading zeros in the version core or in numeric pre-release
+		// identifiers, and pre-release identifiers are never empty and consist
+		// of [0-9A-Za-z-] only.
+		{"1.02.3", plainString},
+		{"1.2.3-01", plainString},
+		{"1.2.3-", plainString},
+		{"1.2.3-rc/1", plainString},
+		{"10.0.0.1", ipAddress},
+		{"::1", ipAddress},
+		{"::ffff:10.0.0.1", ipAddress},
+		{"fe80::1%eth0", ipAddress},
+		{"10.0.0.256", plainString},
+		{"10.0.0.0/8", cidrPrefix},
+		{"::/0", cidrPrefix},
+		{"10.0.0.0/33", plainString},
+		{"2023-01-01", timestamp},
+		{"2023-01-01T15:04:05Z", timestamp},
+		{"2023-01-01T15:04:05.123456789+02:00", timestamp},
+		{"2023-01-01T15:04:05", timestamp},
+		{"2023-01-01 15:04:05", timestamp},
+		{"2023-01-01 15:04:05 +02:00", plainString},
+		{"Mon, 02 Jan 2006 15:04:05 MST", timestamp},
+		{"Mon, 02 Jan 2006 15:04:05 +0200", timestamp},
+		{"2023-13-01", plainString},
+		{"", plainString},
+		{"foo", plainString},
+	} {
+		t.Run(c.value, func(t *testing.T) {
+			require.Equal(t, c.class, parse(c.value).class)
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+// TestCompareMagnitudes makes sure that magnitudes are compared exactly, also
+// beyond the range and the precision of a float64.
+func TestCompareMagnitudes(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, c := range []struct{ smaller, larger string }{
+		{"9007199254740992", "9007199254740993"},
+		{"1.0000000000000000000000001", "1.0000000000000000000000002"},
+		{"1e309", "1e310"},
+		{"-1e310", "-1e309"},
+		{"1e1000000000", "1e1000000001"},
+		{"1e-1000000001", "1e-1000000000"},
+		{"9007199254740992ns", "9007199254740993ns"},
+		{"1e308s", "1e309s"},
+		{"1000000000000000000001B", "1000000000000000000002B"},
+		{"1KB", "1023B"},
+		{"1KB", "1KiB"},
+		{"1e21B", "1YiB"},
+		{"999999999ns", "1s"},
+		{"59.999999999s", "1m"},
+		{"364d", "1y"},
+		{"1e30y", "1.0000000000000000000000001e30y"},
+	} {
+		t.Run(c.smaller+"<"+c.larger, func(t *testing.T) {
+			require.Equal(t, -1, Compare(c.smaller, c.larger))
+			require.Equal(t, +1, Compare(c.larger, c.smaller))
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+// TestCompareEquivalent makes sure that values that are equal within their
+// domain but spelled differently are ordered by their original strings. The
+// cases are listed in the order in which their strings sort.
+func TestCompareEquivalent(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, c := range []struct{ first, second string }{
+		{"1KiB", "1024B"},
+		{"1KB", "1000B"},
+		{"1s", "1000ms"},
+		{"1.0", "1.00"},
+		{"+0", "0"},
+		{"1.0.0", "v1.0.0"},
+		{"1.0.0+a", "1.0.0+b"},
+		{"2001:DB8::1", "2001:db8::1"},
+		{"2023-01-01T00:00:00Z", "2023-01-01T01:00:00+01:00"},
+		{"+Inf", "Inf"},
+	} {
+		t.Run(c.first+"=="+c.second, func(t *testing.T) {
+			require.Equal(t, parse(c.first).class, parse(c.second).class)
+			require.Equal(t, 0, parse(c.first).compare(parse(c.second)))
+			// The original strings break the tie.
+			require.Equal(t, -1, Compare(c.first, c.second))
+			require.Equal(t, +1, Compare(c.second, c.first))
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+func BenchmarkCompare(b *testing.B) {
+	for _, c := range []struct{ name, a, bb string }{
+		{"strings", "node-exporter", "node-exporter-2"},
+		{"numbers", "1234", "1235"},
+		{"durations", "1.5h", "90m"},
+		{"versions", "v1.20.3", "v1.3.0"},
+		{"addresses", "10.0.0.1", "10.0.0.2"},
+	} {
+		b.Run(c.name, func(b *testing.B) {
+			for range b.N {
+				Compare(c.a, c.bb)
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

+// Copyright The Prometheus Authors

+// WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+// See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+// limitations under the License.
+
+package labelsort
+
+import (
+	"cmp"
+	"strings"
+)
+
+// naturalCompare compares a and b in natural sort order, i.e. like a byte-wise
+// comparison except that runs of digits occurring at the same position in both
+// strings are compared by their numeric value ("foo2" sorts before "foo10").
+//
+// Digit runs are compared without converting them to integers, so arbitrarily
+// long runs keep their numeric order. Runs that only differ in leading zeros
+// compare equal, in which case the rest of the strings decides.
+func naturalCompare(a, b string) int {
+	for a != "" && b != "" {
+		if isDigit(a[0]) && isDigit(b[0]) {
+			var runA, runB string
+			runA, a = digitRun(a)
+			runB, b = digitRun(b)
+			if c := compareDigitRuns(runA, runB); c != 0 {
+				return c
+			}
+			continue
+		}
+		if a[0] != b[0] {
+			return cmp.Compare(a[0], b[0])
+		}
+		a, b = a[1:], b[1:]
+	}
+	return cmp.Compare(len(a), len(b))
+}
+
+// digitRun splits off the leading run of digits of s.
+func digitRun(s string) (run, rest string) {
+	i := 0
+	for i < len(s) && isDigit(s[i]) {
+		i++
+	}
+	return s[:i], s[i:]
+}
+
+// compareDigitRuns compares two runs of digits by their numeric value.
+func compareDigitRuns(a, b string) int {
+	a = trimLeadingZeros(a)
+	b = trimLeadingZeros(b)
+	if len(a) != len(b) {
+		return cmp.Compare(len(a), len(b))
+	}
+	return strings.Compare(a, b)
+}
+
+func trimLeadingZeros(s string) string {
+	i := 0
+	for i < len(s) && s[i] == '0' {
+		i++
+	}
+	return s[i:]
+}

+package labelsort
+
+import (
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+func TestNaturalCompare(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, c := range []struct {
+		a, b string
+		want int
+	}{
+		{"", "", 0},
+		{"", "a", -1},
+		{"a", "a", 0},
+		{"a", "b", -1},
+		{"a", "ab", -1},
+		{"A", "a", -1},
+		{"foo2", "foo10", -1},
+		{"foo10", "foo9", 1},
+		{"foo2bar10", "foo2bar9", 1},
+		{"1", "a", -1},
+		{"a1", "ab", -1},
+		{"x1y", "x1", 1},
+		// Digit runs that only differ in leading zeros are equal, the rest of
+		// the strings decides.
+		{"a01", "a1", 0},
+		{"a0009b", "a9b", 0},
+		{"a01b", "a1c", -1},
+		// Long digit runs keep their numeric order.
+		{"1" + strings.Repeat("0", 100), "9" + strings.Repeat("0", 99), 1},
+		{strings.Repeat("9", 100), "1" + strings.Repeat("0", 100), -1},
+	} {
+		t.Run(c.a+"/"+c.b, func(t *testing.T) {
+			require.Equal(t, c.want, naturalCompare(c.a, c.b))
+			require.Equal(t, -c.want, naturalCompare(c.b, c.a))
+		})
+	}
+}
diff --git a/util/labelsort/semver.go b/util/labelsort/semver.go

index 0000000..34e8259
--- /dev/null
+++ b/util/labelsort/semver.go
@@ -0,0 +1,150 @@
+// Copyright The Prometheus Authors
+// Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
+// you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
+// You may obtain a copy of the License at
+//
+// http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0

+// Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
+// distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
+// WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+// See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+// limitations under the License.
+
+package labelsort
+
+import (
+	"cmp"
+	"strings"
+)
+
+// semver is a semantic version as defined by https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html.
+// The version core is kept as digit strings so that arbitrarily large version
+// numbers keep their order.
+type semver struct {
+	major, minor, patch string
+	pre                 string // Pre-release, without the leading '-'.
+}
+
+// parseSemver parses a strict semantic version with an optional leading "v".
+// Anything that is not a complete major.minor.patch version is rejected,
+// including partial versions like "1.2".
+func parseSemver(s string) (semver, bool) {
+	s = strings.TrimPrefix(s, "v")
+
+	if i := strings.IndexByte(s, '+'); i >= 0 {
+		if !validIdentifiers(s[i+1:], false) {
+			return semver{}, false
+		}
+		s = s[:i]
+	}
+	pre := ""
+	if i := strings.IndexByte(s, '-'); i >= 0 {
+		pre = s[i+1:]
+		if !validIdentifiers(pre, true) {
+			return semver{}, false
+		}
+		s = s[:i]
+	}
+
+	major, rest, ok := strings.Cut(s, ".")
+	if !ok {
+		return semver{}, false
+	}
+	minor, patch, ok := strings.Cut(rest, ".")
+	if !ok {
+		return semver{}, false
+	}
+	if !isNumericID(major) || !isNumericID(minor) || !isNumericID(patch) {
+		return semver{}, false
+	}
+	return semver{major: major, minor: minor, patch: patch, pre: pre}, true
+}
+
+// compareSemvers compares two versions by semantic version precedence. Build
+// metadata is ignored, as required by the specification.
+func compareSemvers(a, b semver) int {
+	if c := compareDigitRuns(a.major, b.major); c != 0 {
+		return c
+	}
+	if c := compareDigitRuns(a.minor, b.minor); c != 0 {
+		return c
+	}
+	if c := compareDigitRuns(a.patch, b.patch); c != 0 {
+		return c
+	}
+	return comparePrerelease(a.pre, b.pre)
+}
+
+func comparePrerelease(a, b string) int {
+	switch {
+	case a == b:
+		return 0
+	case a == "": // A release version has higher precedence than a pre-release.
+		return 1
+	case b == "":
+		return -1
+	}
+
+	idsA, idsB := strings.Split(a, "."), strings.Split(b, ".")
+	for i := 0; i < len(idsA) && i < len(idsB); i++ {
+		if c := comparePrereleaseID(idsA[i], idsB[i]); c != 0 {
+			return c
+		}
+	}
+	// A larger set of pre-release fields has a higher precedence.
+	return cmp.Compare(len(idsA), len(idsB))
+}
+
+func comparePrereleaseID(a, b string) int {
+	numA, numB := isNumericID(a), isNumericID(b)
+	switch {
+	case numA && numB:
+		return compareDigitRuns(a, b)
+	case numA: // Numeric identifiers always have lower precedence.
+		return -1
+	case numB:
+		return 1
+	}
+	return strings.Compare(a, b)
+}
+
+// validIdentifiers reports whether s is a dot-separated list of non-empty
+// alphanumeric identifiers. Numeric identifiers of a pre-release must not have
+// leading zeros, those of build metadata may.
+func validIdentifiers(s string, isPrerelease bool) bool {
+	for id := range strings.SplitSeq(s, ".") {
+		if id == "" {
+			return false
+		}
+		numeric := true
+		for i := range len(id) {
+			if c := id[i]; !isDigit(c) {
+				if !isAlpha(c) && c != '-' {
+					return false
+				}
+				numeric = false
+			}
+		}
+		if numeric && isPrerelease && !isNumericID(id) {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return true
+}
+
+// isNumericID reports whether s is a numeric identifier, i.e. digits only and
+// without leading zeros.
+func isNumericID(s string) bool {
+	if s == "" || (len(s) > 1 && s[0] == '0') {
+		return false
+	}
+	for i := range len(s) {
+		if !isDigit(s[i]) {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return true
+}
+
+func isAlpha(c byte) bool { return c >= 'a' && c <= 'z' || c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z' }
diff --git a/util/labelsort/units.go b/util/labelsort/units.go

@@ -0,0 +1,89 @@
+// Copyright The Prometheus Authors

+// WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+// See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+// limitations under the License.
+
+package labelsort
+
+import "strings"
+
+// durationUnits maps the supported duration units to their length in
+// nanoseconds. Duration units are case sensitive, as in Go's time package and
+// in Prometheus' own duration syntax.
+var durationUnits = map[string]decimal{
+	"ns": mustParseDecimal("1"),
+	"us": mustParseDecimal("1e3"),
+	"µs": mustParseDecimal("1e3"), // U+00B5, micro sign.
+	"μs": mustParseDecimal("1e3"), // U+03BC, Greek small letter mu.
+	"ms": mustParseDecimal("1e6"),
+	"s":  mustParseDecimal("1e9"),
+	"m":  mustParseDecimal("60e9"),
+	"h":  mustParseDecimal("3600e9"),
+	"d":  mustParseDecimal("86400e9"),
+	"w":  mustParseDecimal("604800e9"),
+	"y":  mustParseDecimal("31536000e9"), // A year is 365 days, as in Prometheus' duration syntax.
+}
+
+// byteUnits maps the supported byte units to their size in bytes. Byte units
+// are matched case insensitively, so "1kb", "1kB" and "1KB" are all a thousand
+// bytes.
+var byteUnits = map[string]decimal{
+	"b":   mustParseDecimal("1"),
+	"kb":  mustParseDecimal("1e3"),
+	"mb":  mustParseDecimal("1e6"),
+	"gb":  mustParseDecimal("1e9"),
+	"tb":  mustParseDecimal("1e12"),
+	"pb":  mustParseDecimal("1e15"),
+	"eb":  mustParseDecimal("1e18"),
+	"zb":  mustParseDecimal("1e21"),
+	"yb":  mustParseDecimal("1e24"),
+	"kib": mustParseDecimal("1024"),
+	"mib": mustParseDecimal("1048576"),
+	"gib": mustParseDecimal("1073741824"),
+	"tib": mustParseDecimal("1099511627776"),
+	"pib": mustParseDecimal("1125899906842624"),
+	"eib": mustParseDecimal("1152921504606846976"),
+	"zib": mustParseDecimal("1180591620717411303424"),
+	"yib": mustParseDecimal("1208925819614629174706176"),
+}
+
+// maxByteUnitLen is the length of the longest byte unit, used to keep the case
+// folding of unit candidates cheap.
+const maxByteUnitLen = 3
+
+// parseScaled parses a magnitude followed by one of the given units, e.g. a
+// duration like "1.5h" or a size like "-2e3MiB", and returns the magnitude
+// scaled by the unit.
+func parseScaled(s string, units map[string]decimal, foldCase bool) (decimal, bool) {
+	d, unit, ok := parseDecimalPrefix(s)
+	if !ok || unit == "" {
+		return decimal{}, false
+	}
+	if foldCase {
+		if len(unit) > maxByteUnitLen {
+			return decimal{}, false
+		}
+		unit = strings.ToLower(unit)
+	}
+	factor, ok := units[unit]
+	if !ok {
+		return decimal{}, false
+	}
+	return d.mul(factor), true
+}
+
+func mustParseDecimal(s string) decimal {
+	d, rest, ok := parseDecimalPrefix(s)
+	if !ok || rest != "" {
+		panic("labelsort: invalid decimal constant " + s)
+	}
+	return d
+}
